findings.after: - **Role/responsibility:** **Themis owns and manages Harmonia's Authorisation Model**, including PAP, PRP, PDP, Criteria/collections, AuthorisationRoles, Identity assignments, role/group resolution, Criteria compilation and the distributed PEP framework. Themis consumes trusted authenticated Identity; it does not authenticate that Identity. [U12](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u12) refines [U08](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u08) within [AX-07](../../motivation/principle/architectural-axiom/5de2ae2c3b794c2d9f3a14efd51d564f.md). - **PAP — Policy Administration Point:** administration and lifecycle management of the Themis-owned model. Management/review/approval activity uses [Ergo/Praxis and Iris](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/component-register.md#authorisation-administration); detailed Praxes/Erga, UI and versioning mechanisms remain deferred. No general-purpose policy language is implied by policy administration. - **PRP — Policy Repository Point:** authoritative repository semantics for the Authorisation Model. Durable persistence may be delegated through **Themis PRP → Mneme → Mnemosyne Harmonia Configuration & Governance**. This requires no dedicated Themis physical database and transfers no model ownership to persistence. - **PDP — Policy Decision Point:** resolves authoritative policy, authenticated Identity and applicable context into precomputed Identity-specific **PEP-Criteria**, supplied through **PEP-Context** for local enforcement. An immediate decision remains possible; it uses the same governed semantics. - **Governed actions:** **Can I ACCESS XYZ? Can I CHANGE ABC? Can I FORWARD DEF?** ACCESS, CHANGE and FORWARD are distinct; they SHALL NOT collapse into CRUD. FORWARD may depend on destination/context independently of ACCESS. Unauthenticated or unauthorised operations default to **DENY**; unavailable authoritative policy determination remains distinct from that decision. #### Identity.Authentication — separately provided trusted Identity **Identity.Authentication establishes WHO an Individual or System is. It is a Separately Provided Capability (SEP).** The primary pattern is standards-based OIDC/OAuth integration with an externally managed Identity Provider (IdP). Harmonia does not own or provide an identity-management, credential-management, password-management or MFA framework. > **Keycloak + PostgreSQL SHALL provide the default FOSS Identity Provider for > development, test and POC environments.** Keycloak remains an external, replaceable implementation component. Harmonia's Identity.Authentication architecture SHALL NOT acquire Keycloak-specific dependencies. This target does not prescribe a production IdP or an internal Harmonia credential store. Authentication establishes trusted Identity only; it SHALL NOT determine Harmonia Function permissions, Function.Scope or PEP-Criteria. **Identity.Authorisation** establishes what that authenticated Identity may do within Harmonia and is Themis-owned. The same authorisation model applies to human and system Identities; differing allowable assignments do not establish separate architectures. #### Identity and role terminology | Term | Candidate meaning and boundary | | :--- | :--- | | **Identity** | The authenticated Individual or System consumed by Themis. This use does not redefine Information Unit Identity or the Domain04 professional identifier assertions. | | **Practitioner** | The individual practitioner, retaining the [Domain04 workforce-entity meaning](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/practitioner.md#31-practitioner); registration status is a separate assertion. | | **FHIR PractitionerRole** | The formal practitioner role/service relationship represented through FHIR. | | **PractitionerCapacity** | The selected operational capacity in which a Practitioner is currently acting within Harmonia; it does not itself confer authority. | | **AuthorisationRole** | A named, governed, assignable collection of additive Themis Criteria and/or Criteria collections. It is distinct from PractitionerCapacity, FHIR PractitionerRole and a Domain03 Business Role. | | **Criterion / Criteria** | One governed permitted combination / multiple such combinations in the Themis Authorisation Model. | | **PEP-Criteria** | The precomputed, Identity-specific set of permitted combinations derived by Themis for constrained local enforcement. | | **PEP-Context** | The Themis-derived operational enforcement context for an authenticated Identity, through which applicable PEP-Criteria is supplied. It is distinct from the general Mneme working Context. | The [Domain04 Practitioner Role Binding](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/practitioner.md#36-practitioner-role-binding) and [Domain03 Business Roles](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/actors-roles/roles.md) retain their meanings. Neither lexical similarity nor FHIR convention establishes their mapping to PractitionerCapacity or AuthorisationRole. #### Criterion conjunction and additive grants A Criterion represents a **governed permitted combination** across applicable dimensions, using [Calliope-controlled nomenclature](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/component-register.md#authorisation-nomenclature): ```text Criterion = Information.Compartment AND Information.Classification AND Function.Name AND Function.Scope AND applicable Temporal constraints ``` The four principal dimensions describe **what** is authorised; applicable temporal constraints describe **when**. Within an individual Criterion, applicable dimensions are **conjunctive**. Between Criteria, grants are **additive / UNION**: each Criterion independently contributes its permitted combination. Only explicitly governed combinations have authorisation meaning. Absence of a matching effective Criterion results in **DENY**. **Explicit negative/DENY Criteria are not part of this Candidate Architecture.** Neither arbitrary Boolean policy expressions, deny-overrides semantics nor a general-purpose policy language is introduced by this model. #### Criteria containment, AuthorisationRoles and Identity assignments Criteria support containment, collection and nesting for management and reuse: ```text CriteriaCollection (conceptual label; final name unresolved) ├── Criterion ├── Criterion └── CriteriaCollection ├── Criterion └── Criterion ``` Flattening nested collections produces the same additive set of effective Criteria. Nesting creates no arbitrary Boolean semantics and requires no Role hierarchy. The exact implementation name/class hierarchy and representation remain deferred; this diagram establishes no lifecycle/ownership semantics beyond the stated management/reuse requirement. An **AuthorisationRole** is named, governed and assignable and contains Criteria and/or Criteria collections. Its contents are additive: ```text EffectiveCriteria(AuthorisationRole) = UNION(all contained Criteria) IdentityEffectiveCriteria = DirectCriteria UNION AuthorisationRole1.Criteria UNION AuthorisationRole2.Criteria UNION ... ``` An Identity may have directly assigned Criteria, one or more AuthorisationRoles, or both. This applies to human and system Identities. The UNION is of applicable grants, subject to governed assignments, temporal validity, revocation and applicable operational context; it does not remove a Criterion's conjunctions or require every contained Criterion to match simultaneously. #### Predetermined temporal validity and explicit revocation **Temporal validity** establishes predetermined applicability/validity bounds. Temporal constraints may apply to a Criterion, a direct Criterion assignment, an AuthorisationRole assignment and applicable operational context such as PractitionerCapacity. The exact temporal expression model remains deferred. **Revocation** withdraws an otherwise valid authorisation. It SHALL NOT be modelled merely as temporal expiry. Both concepts are required. Propagation of revocation and invalidation of already-issued PEP-Criteria/PEP-Context remain unresolved; no mechanism or continued validity after revocation is inferred. #### PractitionerCapacity and operational responsibility For a Practitioner, the available PractitionerCapacity set is constrained by the practitioner's governed profile and applicable operational context. The Practitioner selects **one active PractitionerCapacity** for the applicable session/operational or roster context. It supplies operational context used by Themis when deriving effective authorisation; **it does not itself confer authority**. Selection UI and the exact PractitionerCapacity ↔ FHIR PractitionerRole mapping remain deferred. > **Authentication establishes who the Individual is. PractitionerCapacity > establishes the capacity in which a Practitioner is currently acting. Themis > establishes what that Identity, acting in that capacity, may do.** ```mermaid graph TD Auth["Authenticated Practitioner"] --> Eligible["Eligible PractitionerCapacity set"] Profile["Governed practitioner profile"] --> Eligible Context["Applicable operational / roster context"] --> Eligible Eligible -->|"Practitioner selects ONE"| Capacity["Active PractitionerCapacity: context, no authority by itself"] Capacity -->|"authorisation context"| PDP["Themis: resolve governed Criteria / assignments / policy state"] PDP --> Criteria["Identity-specific precomputed PEP-Criteria through PEP-Context"] Criteria --> PEP["Constrained local Themis PEP"] Capacity -.->|"operational responsibility context"| Responsibility["Agora: membership intent; detailed context use deferred"] ``` Themis answers **“May this Identity perform this action on this information?”** Future Agora collaboration detail concerns **“Is this Practitioner currently responsible for receiving/responding to this operational activity?”** These are separate responsibilities even where they consume the same PractitionerCapacity. Receipt of an escalation or approval notification grants no information access. Following it into Iris or another application surface requires normal Themis PEP enforcement using current valid PEP-Criteria. U16 establishes [Agora control and Omilia operations](d1c4053e68384080b8eb79d2008632ba.md); detailed membership, escalation and approval-routing mechanics remain deferred. #### PEP-Context and distributed enforcement > **PEP-Context is the Themis-derived policy enforcement context established for > an authenticated Identity. It supplies the precomputed PEP-Criteria applicable > to that Identity that a Themis Policy Enforcement Point requires for local > enforcement decisions.** **PEP-Criteria is a precomputed, Identity-specific set of permitted combinations**, not a general-purpose executable policy language distributed to PEPs. Themis resolves direct Criteria, AuthorisationRole-derived Criteria, nested collections, applicable temporal constraints, PractitionerCapacity context where applicable and authoritative policy state. PEPs SHALL NOT receive the complete model merely because they need enforcement information. ```text Policy Authorisation Model managed by Themis Criteria governed permitted combinations in the Authorisation Model PEP-Criteria precomputed Identity-specific permitted combinations PEP-Context operational context supplying applicable PEP-Criteria Enforcement Decision local PEP determination for a particular proposed action ``` Enforcement occurs at the component capable of preventing the action. A PEP may be a Themis-provided library/framework element embedded within a host module. **The distributed PEP capability, implementation and enforcement semantics are Themis-owned/derived/built.** The host controls the actual operation; Themis supplies enforcement mechanism and semantics. Hosts SHALL NOT independently reinterpret the Authorisation Model in place of the Themis PEP. No separate central Policy Enforcement Software Component is created. A local PEP SHALL perform deliberately **constrained, deterministic enforcement** against authenticated Identity context, effective Information.Compartment and Information.Classification, Function.Name, Function.Scope, applicable temporal state and the Identity's valid PEP-Criteria. It SHALL NOT become a general-purpose policy interpreter. Themis SHALL retain sufficient provenance to explain effective PEP-Criteria derivation: authoritative Criteria, collections, direct/AuthorisationRole assignments and applicable policy state. Runtime PEP-Criteria need not carry the full derivation history; stable references may support it. No final wire/data structure, cache, refresh or distribution mechanism is prescribed. PEP-Context and existing security-context contracts are operational context; they do not automatically become persisted resource content. Their detailed relationship, schema and distribution mechanisms remain unresolved; PEP-Context is not silently equated with a historical class or transport carrier. #### Untagged information and effective security attributes > **Absence of explicit information security metadata does not imply absence > of security control. Untagged information is not unrestricted information.** Where required Information.Compartment and/or Information.Classification attributes are absent, effective values SHALL be established through governed, deterministic rules. If required effective attributes cannot be established, enforcement SHALL fail closed. Deriving effective attributes for an authorisation decision is distinct from persistently assigning/changing security metadata on an Information Unit. Themis enforces the resulting attributes; it is not assumed to own all semantic derivation rules. Exact derivation ownership and precedence, including possible context/containment relationships, remain [deferred](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#identity-deferred-design). Mnemosyne's established compartment validation/reapplication responsibility does not settle those semantic rules. #### Availability and delegation An in-flight activity with a **valid PEP-Context sufficient for its required enforcement decisions** may continue during temporary PDP unavailability. PDP availability is required for a **new, renewed or replacement PEP-Context**. If the PDP cannot establish that required context, the activity SHALL NOT proceed beyond the point requiring it and must wait. **PDP unavailability is not policy denial**: policy permits, policy denies, and authoritative policy determination cannot presently be established remain distinct. This grants no unauthenticated or unauthorised action permission and weakens no required audit-capture boundary. Detailed validity, timeout/retry, revocation and renewal mechanisms are unresolved. At this stage delegation is **Identity / PEP-Criteria pass-off (forwarding)**, subject to applicable **FORWARD** authority. Provenance SHALL preserve both the originating Identity and receiving/acting Identity; the receiver does not become the originator. No separate general-purpose delegation subsystem is introduced. Detailed forwarding lifecycle/representation, PDP interaction and governance mechanisms remain deferred; forwarding establishes no unrestricted impersonation or authority-broadening rule. #### Governed authorisation administration and target allocation Authorisation administration is governed Harmonia work. Criteria creation/change, collection management, AuthorisationRole management, direct Identity Criteria assignment, AuthorisationRole assignment, temporal changes and revocation SHALL be subject to appropriate governed management/review/approval processes through **Ergo/Praxis**, with **Iris** providing human interaction. Detailed PAP management Praxes/Erga and approval rules remain deferred; this does not make every change require an identical approval sequence. | Responsibility | Candidate target | | :--- | :--- | | Identity authentication | Keycloak / external OIDC IdP; SEP, Keycloak + PostgreSQL default for development/test/POC | | Controlled authorisation nomenclature | Calliope | | Authorisation model, Criteria/collections, AuthorisationRoles and Identity assignments | Themis-owned | | Role/group resolution | Themis-owned; no separate human/system authorisation architecture | | Criteria compilation | Themis-owned | | Policy repository | Themis PRP, persisted through Harmonia via Mneme / Mnemosyne C&G | | Policy administration | Themis PAP | | Governed management / review / approval workflows | Ergo/Praxis | | Administration UI | Iris; no authorisation-model ownership or detailed reusable-form design | | Runtime enforcement | Themis PEP library at action-controlling hosts | | Untagged information handling | Governed effective-attribute resolution; exact ownership/precedence deferred | Harmonia owns its authorisation semantics. **jCasbin, OPA, Cedar or another general-purpose policy framework is not an architectural dependency.** FOSS implementations may later supply implementation references where appropriate; their conceptual models SHALL NOT redefine Harmonia semantics. - **Collaboration/exclusions:** governed access, activity, publication and collaboration hosts use Themis-owned PEP capability. Petasos hosts governed FORWARD enforcement because it controls the queue operation. Praxis may supply relevant context but is not the Authorisation Model; authorisation does not establish Praxis conformance. Themis is neither Audit nor Assurance. Significant policy/enforcement occurrences are reported through Kleio Audit Capture under applicable policy; clients need not construct FHIR AuditEvent. **Calliope defines security/assurance nomenclature; Themis decides/enforces; Dokimasia assures; Kleio audits.** Governance, Authorisation, Assurance and Audit remain distinct responsibilities; Praxis conformance and assurance findings are not authorisation grants. findings.before: - **Role/responsibility:** **Themis owns and manages Harmonia's Authorisation Model**, including PAP, PRP, PDP, Criteria/collections, AuthorisationRoles, Identity assignments, role/group resolution, Criteria compilation and the distributed PEP framework. Themis consumes trusted authenticated Identity; it does not authenticate that Identity. [U12](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u12) refines [U08](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/sources.md#u08) within [AX-07](../../motivation/principle/5de2ae2c3b794c2d9f3a14efd51d564f.md). - **PAP — Policy Administration Point:** administration and lifecycle management of the Themis-owned model. Management/review/approval activity uses [Ergo/Praxis and Iris](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/component-register.md#authorisation-administration); detailed Praxes/Erga, UI and versioning mechanisms remain deferred. No general-purpose policy language is implied by policy administration. - **PRP — Policy Repository Point:** authoritative repository semantics for the Authorisation Model. Durable persistence may be delegated through **Themis PRP → Mneme → Mnemosyne Harmonia Configuration & Governance**. This requires no dedicated Themis physical database and transfers no model ownership to persistence. - **PDP — Policy Decision Point:** resolves authoritative policy, authenticated Identity and applicable context into precomputed Identity-specific **PEP-Criteria**, supplied through **PEP-Context** for local enforcement. An immediate decision remains possible; it uses the same governed semantics. - **Governed actions:** **Can I ACCESS XYZ? Can I CHANGE ABC? Can I FORWARD DEF?** ACCESS, CHANGE and FORWARD are distinct; they SHALL NOT collapse into CRUD. FORWARD may depend on destination/context independently of ACCESS. Unauthenticated or unauthorised operations default to **DENY**; unavailable authoritative policy determination remains distinct from that decision. #### Identity.Authentication — separately provided trusted Identity **Identity.Authentication establishes WHO an Individual or System is. It is a Separately Provided Capability (SEP).** The primary pattern is standards-based OIDC/OAuth integration with an externally managed Identity Provider (IdP). Harmonia does not own or provide an identity-management, credential-management, password-management or MFA framework. > **Keycloak + PostgreSQL SHALL provide the default FOSS Identity Provider for > development, test and POC environments.** Keycloak remains an external, replaceable implementation component. Harmonia's Identity.Authentication architecture SHALL NOT acquire Keycloak-specific dependencies. This target does not prescribe a production IdP or an internal Harmonia credential store. Authentication establishes trusted Identity only; it SHALL NOT determine Harmonia Function permissions, Function.Scope or PEP-Criteria. **Identity.Authorisation** establishes what that authenticated Identity may do within Harmonia and is Themis-owned. The same authorisation model applies to human and system Identities; differing allowable assignments do not establish separate architectures. #### Identity and role terminology | Term | Candidate meaning and boundary | | :--- | :--- | | **Identity** | The authenticated Individual or System consumed by Themis. This use does not redefine Information Unit Identity or the Domain04 professional identifier assertions. | | **Practitioner** | The individual practitioner, retaining the [Domain04 workforce-entity meaning](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/practitioner.md#31-practitioner); registration status is a separate assertion. | | **FHIR PractitionerRole** | The formal practitioner role/service relationship represented through FHIR. | | **PractitionerCapacity** | The selected operational capacity in which a Practitioner is currently acting within Harmonia; it does not itself confer authority. | | **AuthorisationRole** | A named, governed, assignable collection of additive Themis Criteria and/or Criteria collections. It is distinct from PractitionerCapacity, FHIR PractitionerRole and a Domain03 Business Role. | | **Criterion / Criteria** | One governed permitted combination / multiple such combinations in the Themis Authorisation Model. | | **PEP-Criteria** | The precomputed, Identity-specific set of permitted combinations derived by Themis for constrained local enforcement. | | **PEP-Context** | The Themis-derived operational enforcement context for an authenticated Identity, through which applicable PEP-Criteria is supplied. It is distinct from the general Mneme working Context. | The [Domain04 Practitioner Role Binding](../../../../docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/practitioner.md#36-practitioner-role-binding) and [Domain03 Business Roles](../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/actors-roles/roles.md) retain their meanings. Neither lexical similarity nor FHIR convention establishes their mapping to PractitionerCapacity or AuthorisationRole. #### Criterion conjunction and additive grants A Criterion represents a **governed permitted combination** across applicable dimensions, using [Calliope-controlled nomenclature](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/component-register.md#authorisation-nomenclature): ```text Criterion = Information.Compartment AND Information.Classification AND Function.Name AND Function.Scope AND applicable Temporal constraints ``` The four principal dimensions describe **what** is authorised; applicable temporal constraints describe **when**. Within an individual Criterion, applicable dimensions are **conjunctive**. Between Criteria, grants are **additive / UNION**: each Criterion independently contributes its permitted combination. Only explicitly governed combinations have authorisation meaning. Absence of a matching effective Criterion results in **DENY**. **Explicit negative/DENY Criteria are not part of this Candidate Architecture.** Neither arbitrary Boolean policy expressions, deny-overrides semantics nor a general-purpose policy language is introduced by this model. #### Criteria containment, AuthorisationRoles and Identity assignments Criteria support containment, collection and nesting for management and reuse: ```text CriteriaCollection (conceptual label; final name unresolved) ├── Criterion ├── Criterion └── CriteriaCollection ├── Criterion └── Criterion ``` Flattening nested collections produces the same additive set of effective Criteria. Nesting creates no arbitrary Boolean semantics and requires no Role hierarchy. The exact implementation name/class hierarchy and representation remain deferred; this diagram establishes no lifecycle/ownership semantics beyond the stated management/reuse requirement. An **AuthorisationRole** is named, governed and assignable and contains Criteria and/or Criteria collections. Its contents are additive: ```text EffectiveCriteria(AuthorisationRole) = UNION(all contained Criteria) IdentityEffectiveCriteria = DirectCriteria UNION AuthorisationRole1.Criteria UNION AuthorisationRole2.Criteria UNION ... ``` An Identity may have directly assigned Criteria, one or more AuthorisationRoles, or both. This applies to human and system Identities. The UNION is of applicable grants, subject to governed assignments, temporal validity, revocation and applicable operational context; it does not remove a Criterion's conjunctions or require every contained Criterion to match simultaneously. #### Predetermined temporal validity and explicit revocation **Temporal validity** establishes predetermined applicability/validity bounds. Temporal constraints may apply to a Criterion, a direct Criterion assignment, an AuthorisationRole assignment and applicable operational context such as PractitionerCapacity. The exact temporal expression model remains deferred. **Revocation** withdraws an otherwise valid authorisation. It SHALL NOT be modelled merely as temporal expiry. Both concepts are required. Propagation of revocation and invalidation of already-issued PEP-Criteria/PEP-Context remain unresolved; no mechanism or continued validity after revocation is inferred. #### PractitionerCapacity and operational responsibility For a Practitioner, the available PractitionerCapacity set is constrained by the practitioner's governed profile and applicable operational context. The Practitioner selects **one active PractitionerCapacity** for the applicable session/operational or roster context. It supplies operational context used by Themis when deriving effective authorisation; **it does not itself confer authority**. Selection UI and the exact PractitionerCapacity ↔ FHIR PractitionerRole mapping remain deferred. > **Authentication establishes who the Individual is. PractitionerCapacity > establishes the capacity in which a Practitioner is currently acting. Themis > establishes what that Identity, acting in that capacity, may do.** ```mermaid graph TD Auth["Authenticated Practitioner"] --> Eligible["Eligible PractitionerCapacity set"] Profile["Governed practitioner profile"] --> Eligible Context["Applicable operational / roster context"] --> Eligible Eligible -->|"Practitioner selects ONE"| Capacity["Active PractitionerCapacity: context, no authority by itself"] Capacity -->|"authorisation context"| PDP["Themis: resolve governed Criteria / assignments / policy state"] PDP --> Criteria["Identity-specific precomputed PEP-Criteria through PEP-Context"] Criteria --> PEP["Constrained local Themis PEP"] Capacity -.->|"operational responsibility context"| Responsibility["Agora: membership intent; detailed context use deferred"] ``` Themis answers **“May this Identity perform this action on this information?”** Future Agora collaboration detail concerns **“Is this Practitioner currently responsible for receiving/responding to this operational activity?”** These are separate responsibilities even where they consume the same PractitionerCapacity. Receipt of an escalation or approval notification grants no information access. Following it into Iris or another application surface requires normal Themis PEP enforcement using current valid PEP-Criteria. U16 establishes [Agora control and Omilia operations](d1c4053e68384080b8eb79d2008632ba.md); detailed membership, escalation and approval-routing mechanics remain deferred. #### PEP-Context and distributed enforcement > **PEP-Context is the Themis-derived policy enforcement context established for > an authenticated Identity. It supplies the precomputed PEP-Criteria applicable > to that Identity that a Themis Policy Enforcement Point requires for local > enforcement decisions.** **PEP-Criteria is a precomputed, Identity-specific set of permitted combinations**, not a general-purpose executable policy language distributed to PEPs. Themis resolves direct Criteria, AuthorisationRole-derived Criteria, nested collections, applicable temporal constraints, PractitionerCapacity context where applicable and authoritative policy state. PEPs SHALL NOT receive the complete model merely because they need enforcement information. ```text Policy Authorisation Model managed by Themis Criteria governed permitted combinations in the Authorisation Model PEP-Criteria precomputed Identity-specific permitted combinations PEP-Context operational context supplying applicable PEP-Criteria Enforcement Decision local PEP determination for a particular proposed action ``` Enforcement occurs at the component capable of preventing the action. A PEP may be a Themis-provided library/framework element embedded within a host module. **The distributed PEP capability, implementation and enforcement semantics are Themis-owned/derived/built.** The host controls the actual operation; Themis supplies enforcement mechanism and semantics. Hosts SHALL NOT independently reinterpret the Authorisation Model in place of the Themis PEP. No separate central Policy Enforcement Software Component is created. A local PEP SHALL perform deliberately **constrained, deterministic enforcement** against authenticated Identity context, effective Information.Compartment and Information.Classification, Function.Name, Function.Scope, applicable temporal state and the Identity's valid PEP-Criteria. It SHALL NOT become a general-purpose policy interpreter. Themis SHALL retain sufficient provenance to explain effective PEP-Criteria derivation: authoritative Criteria, collections, direct/AuthorisationRole assignments and applicable policy state. Runtime PEP-Criteria need not carry the full derivation history; stable references may support it. No final wire/data structure, cache, refresh or distribution mechanism is prescribed. PEP-Context and existing security-context contracts are operational context; they do not automatically become persisted resource content. Their detailed relationship, schema and distribution mechanisms remain unresolved; PEP-Context is not silently equated with a historical class or transport carrier. #### Untagged information and effective security attributes > **Absence of explicit information security metadata does not imply absence > of security control. Untagged information is not unrestricted information.** Where required Information.Compartment and/or Information.Classification attributes are absent, effective values SHALL be established through governed, deterministic rules. If required effective attributes cannot be established, enforcement SHALL fail closed. Deriving effective attributes for an authorisation decision is distinct from persistently assigning/changing security metadata on an Information Unit. Themis enforces the resulting attributes; it is not assumed to own all semantic derivation rules. Exact derivation ownership and precedence, including possible context/containment relationships, remain [deferred](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/gaps.md#identity-deferred-design). Mnemosyne's established compartment validation/reapplication responsibility does not settle those semantic rules. #### Availability and delegation An in-flight activity with a **valid PEP-Context sufficient for its required enforcement decisions** may continue during temporary PDP unavailability. PDP availability is required for a **new, renewed or replacement PEP-Context**. If the PDP cannot establish that required context, the activity SHALL NOT proceed beyond the point requiring it and must wait. **PDP unavailability is not policy denial**: policy permits, policy denies, and authoritative policy determination cannot presently be established remain distinct. This grants no unauthenticated or unauthorised action permission and weakens no required audit-capture boundary. Detailed validity, timeout/retry, revocation and renewal mechanisms are unresolved. At this stage delegation is **Identity / PEP-Criteria pass-off (forwarding)**, subject to applicable **FORWARD** authority. Provenance SHALL preserve both the originating Identity and receiving/acting Identity; the receiver does not become the originator. No separate general-purpose delegation subsystem is introduced. Detailed forwarding lifecycle/representation, PDP interaction and governance mechanisms remain deferred; forwarding establishes no unrestricted impersonation or authority-broadening rule. #### Governed authorisation administration and target allocation Authorisation administration is governed Harmonia work. Criteria creation/change, collection management, AuthorisationRole management, direct Identity Criteria assignment, AuthorisationRole assignment, temporal changes and revocation SHALL be subject to appropriate governed management/review/approval processes through **Ergo/Praxis**, with **Iris** providing human interaction. Dokimasia provides this reusable architectural library responsibility for use by
Harmonia components and execution activities. It performs the common work of
Provenance creation, capture of relevant information/activity/context references,
and reporting or publishing Provenance into the Provenance Management framework.
The originating component generates Provenance through the library; Dokimasia
retains ownership of the framework and management/lifecycle of resulting information.

This is a logical ApplicationComponent representing the agreed reusable library,
not an implementation-level Java class/interface, additional execution framework,
runtime service or deployment boundary. Provision by Dokimasia asserts no runtime
containment, Java dependency or particular contract/transport. Existing Ponos,
Ergo/Ergon and governed information-management facilities remain in use.

Provenance references relevant InformationUnits, Pragma instances, execution
activities and associated Context without requiring embedded contents. Existing
identity/version/reference/governance semantics remain unchanged. Management uses
Mneme and authoritative durable persistence uses Mnemosyne; the library establishes
no independent storage and does not make publication success equivalent to persistence
or Assurance. It grants no assured component control over Assurance conclusions.
Kleio's Audit capture contract/library and AuditEvent responsibilities remain separate.

agreed intent is not formal candidate acceptance. Original versus linked new retry
Pragma, attempt representation, synchronous/asynchronous publication, acknowledgement/
recovery, Provenance schemas/cardinalities/lifecycle states and detailed client-library
contracts/deployment remain unresolved. No implementation is authorised.

findings.after:
This axiom is maintained in this register. Current Harmonia realisation describes downstream machinery and is non-normative.

#### Axiom
> **Operational activity associated with a real-world entity progresses through explicit and observable state transitions coordinated with the governed state of that entity. Operational activity is not treated merely as a sequence of disconnected message transfers.**

#### Architectural Implications
- Health integration involves multi-stage workflows (e.g., ADT distribution, lab specimen processing).
- Operational tasks must be tracked in lockstep with the real-world state of the clinical entity.
- Prevents silent destination divergence during fan-out processing: every destination hop is an observable sub-state of the parent operational activity.

#### Current Harmonia Realisation (Non-Normative)
- Implemented in `energeia-erga` (e.g., `AdtDistributionErgon` tracking destination fan-out checkpoints).
- Multi-destination statuses (`FANOUT_DISPATCH_INITIATED`, `QUEUED`, `DELIVERED`) are recorded in Pragma envelopes and FHIR `Task.output` extensions.

#### Approved interpretation and related authority

The 2026-10-09 migration adjudication preserves coordinated, explicit and
observable progression. The "lockstep" implication above does not mandate
synchronous execution, atomic entity/activity updates or a literal lockstep
implementation. AX-16 does not require universal Digital Twin routing, a Twin
for population/search activity, or clinical-work authority.

The [Strategy entity-specific Digital Twin coordination rule](../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/strategic-views/logical-component-responsibilities.md#entity-specific-operational-coordination)
remains the controlling Strategy-level specialisation of AX-16.
[AX-18](architectural-axiom/b8cafe3cf5904d2bb9a9767260fddf78.md) constrains inference of domain authority from coordination.

findings.after:
**Description**
Information describing the governed resolution of a Task, including its completion disposition, resulting information and applicable outputs.

> **TaskOutcome is the governed resolution of an ActionableTask according to
> that ActionableTask's explicitly defined outcome policy.**

TaskOutcome belongs to and resolves the ActionableTask. It does not
independently belong to a FulfillmentTask. Conceptually it:

- **references FulfillmentTask [0..*]**: identifies the undertaking or
  undertakings that participated in establishing the outcome, as determined
  by `OutcomeConcurrency.Mode`;
- **contains Task Completion Metadata**: Harmonia-governed information
  concerning resolution/completion of the ActionableTask; no complete
  metadata schema is defined here; and
- **contains / represents Task.Output(s)**: the resulting ActionableTask
  output established from the participating undertakings' outputs according
  to `Outcome.OutputRules.Mode`.

The encapsulated domain content of a `Task.Output` may remain semantically
opaque to Harmonia. Neither output information nor TaskOutcome becomes the
physical, clinical or other phenomenon represented. No detailed Task.Output
payload structure is established here.

**Recursive TaskOutcome containment is excluded from this model.** Multiple
execution results are represented through references from the single
governed TaskOutcome to the relevant participating FulfillmentTask
undertakings, rather than through recursive outcome aggregation hierarchies.
Aggregate participation does not imply recursive composition. The remaining
questions in §5 remain unresolved.

Source standing: Bounded adjudicated conceptual Task meaning; section 5 reservations, including runtime TaskOutcome identity/lifecycle, remain unresolved.

Under [AX-17](../../../motivation/principle/architectural-axiom/8882573df7ce43c6bc0f66da0a676139.md), the following
remaining Task / Work matters require subsequent architectural adjudication
or separately governed detailed definition:

- TaskOutcome identity rules;
- detailed cardinalities beyond the established relationships, including
  whether an outcome is mandatory;
- detailed TaskOutcome lifecycle/state semantics;
- detailed Task Completion Metadata and Task.Output payload structures, and
  their representation mechanisms;
- detailed finishing/qualification rules, assignment mechanisms and
  concurrency execution mechanics; and
- task-specific explicit output rules and their downstream execution
  mechanisms.

Outcome ownership, participation modes, output-rule modes, their orthogonality
and exclusion of recursive TaskOutcome composition are adjudicated above;
they SHALL NOT be presented as still provisional or unresolved. This
refinement allocates no previously unestablished archetype-authoring or
outcome-authority owner.

**ReportedTask remains unresolved.** Its existing intersection with
Definition → Contextualisation → Fulfilment → Outcome → Accountability does
not reaffirm its previous definition or require a separate accountable report.
Its necessity and semantics may overlap accountability, assurance, audit,
historical representation and evidence, and require separate adjudication.
It is neither removed nor normalised into one of those concerns here. No
ReportedTask relationships, identity, immutability or lifecycle are settled.

The metamodel, reusable pattern and general lifecycle/containment guidance
SHALL NOT be used to fill these reserved questions by inference. The bounded
semantics above are established; the remaining Task / Work family and Domain04
are not declared complete.

### Outcome Definition
Sensitive health information is demonstrably safeguarded across all integration operations, backed by default-deny authorization, zero-PHI diagnostic logging, and tamper-evident audit provenance that satisfies rigorous statutory data protection regimes.

### Clinical & Operational Value
- **Patient Trust & Confidentiality**: Patients are assured that their intimate health data is protected from unauthorized access, eavesdropping, and accidental leakage into operational logs.
- **Statutory Compliance & Legal Assurance**: The regional health network demonstrably complies with national privacy legislation (e.g., the Australian *Privacy Act 1988*, My Health Records Act, and Notifiable Data Breaches scheme), eliminating legal liability and multi-million-dollar breach penalties.
- **Forensic Auditability**: Every state-changing clinical transaction maintains unambiguous, tamper-evident cryptographic provenance (who authorized it, what information was conveyed, when it occurred), enabling rigorous clinical incident retrospectives.

### Relationship to Motivational Principles
Unlike Outcomes O1 and O2 (which receive direct handovers from specific strategic goals), Outcome O3 is an **intrinsic platform property**:
- It is realized through the foundational architectural principles [AX-07 (Security Is Intrinsic to Managed Operations)](../principle/architectural-axiom/5de2ae2c3b794c2d9f3a14efd51d564f.md) and [AX-08 (Evidence Records Meaning)](../principle/21d6864657964ba5b03e3f6b5eb29cd5.md).
- Security and privacy are enforced intrinsically across all governed ingress, processing, and egress paths rather than being isolated to a single integration workflow.
- As established in the [Orientation View](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/orientation-view.md), AX-07 and AX-08 do not maintain causal arrows to outcomes; O3 acts as a common consequence sink for the entire platform.

Provenance is governed information describing where/how information arose and the
activities associated with its creation, use or progression. It preserves origin
and processing history without conferring Information Authority. This DataObject
represents the Provenance information concept already described by existing
information-governance assertions; it adds no competing lineage or Assurance concept.

**Management and persistence:** [Dokimasia](../application-component/d739c75dffe2453081735710b285f03b.md)
owns the Provenance Management framework and lifecycle. Originating components
and execution activities generate this information using the Dokimasia-provided
Provenance Client Library. [Mneme](../application-component/1af8a56358f7429fabfb57be66542a99.md)
provides governed information management and [Mnemosyne](../application-component/7985e647bf9e4ca3ba70faf9e3e4ae02.md)
provides authoritative durable persistence using existing mechanisms. No independent
Provenance persistence subsystem is established. Ownership, custody and physical
persistence remain distinct; reliability, durability and timely information management
remain governed by existing requirements, including AX-05/10/11.

**References:** Records reference relevant [InformationUnits](class/74ec609de1ae498fbf9d13e4ef8c6cbe.md),
[Pragma instances](27ad143e7c784e378556af8a57c438f7.md), execution activities and
[associated Context](76ded4866bf443dabc0849d68b215690.md). References to activity
performed by [Ergon](../application-component/49c9eb2bef0c47b8b5328621d5fc5479.md)
do not turn Ergon itself into an Information Resource. Information contents need
not be embedded. Existing identity, versioning, information-reference and governance
semantics remain authoritative; these associations prescribe no reference schema,
cardinality, execution-attempt identity or lifecycle state.

**Assurance:** Provenance is foundational evidence used by Dokimasia when evaluating
governed activities and information against applicable assurance obligations.
Observed activity/evidence, Provenance describing it, applicable assurance basis,
and assessment/findings/outcomes remain distinct. [Praxis](0f961462340348b290fd844357d54d67.md)
remains the assurance basis; [Journey](359b901df27f4b43b5a2ff14a8484e34.md) remains
the observed-progression evidence subject, without becoming a complete Provenance
graph. Provenance availability does not itself establish an assurance conclusion;
insufficient evidence remains explicit under REQ-FND-005. Originating-component
evidence generation gives it no authority to determine, suppress, manufacture or
alter its own Assurance outcome.

**Audit boundary:** [Kleio](../application-component/fefda110e2274884ad58906733606efd.md)
retains Audit information management and historical audit evidence. Provenance
and AuditEvents remain distinct; audit evidence may contribute to Assurance without
making Kleio the assessment engine. Existing meaningful-evidence and ephemeral-state
rules (AX-08/09) still apply; routine mechanics are not automatically durable evidence.
The existing finite Dokimasia assurance boundary and absence of a separate own-execution
AuditEvent are preserved, without establishing a recursive assurance requirement.

**Standing and unresolved detail:** The Task records agreed responsibilities;
this representation is an ADD candidate awaiting Solution Architect acceptance under
HCRL 1.1.19-001 DR-18/DR-19. Retry original versus linked new Pragma, execution-attempt
representation, synchronous/asynchronous reporting, publication acknowledgement and
recovery, detailed schemas/cardinalities/lifecycle states and detailed client-library
contracts/deployment remain unresolved. These questions are not prerequisites for
representing the agreed responsibilities. No FHIR representation, information family,
transport, API, database or deployment model is selected.

findings.after:
#### Axiom

> Harmonia MAY integrate information concerning, and coordinate operational activity associated with, an externally governed domain activity without thereby acquiring authority to determine or manage that domain activity.
>
> Authority to determine or manage a domain activity SHALL remain with the responsible actor, system or governed capability unless that authority is explicitly assigned to Harmonia by the architecture.
>
> Harmonia's observation, processing, persistence, distribution, presentation or use of information concerning a domain activity SHALL NOT, by itself, establish authority over that activity.

#### Rationale

Participation in a domain activity and authority over that activity are
different architectural concerns. Information possession, observation,
integration, coordination and processing do not, by themselves, confer
domain authority. Authority requires explicit architectural assignment.

This new human-approved axiom generalises an already-established class of
architectural boundary. It is established at the 2026-10-09 migration
boundary; it is not a claim that AX-01 through AX-17 always contained this
axiom.

#### Consequences and qualifications

AX-18 SHALL NOT be interpreted as preventing Harmonia from performing
operational activity for which architecture has assigned Harmonia
responsibility. Explicit architectural assignment may establish authority
to determine or manage a domain activity.

In particular, AX-18 does not mean:

- Harmonia cannot execute Praxis/Ergo activity;
- Harmonia cannot coordinate entity-specific operational activity through a Digital Twin;
- Harmonia cannot process or transform clinical information;
- Harmonia cannot perform workflow/activity coordination;
- Harmonia cannot manage responsibilities explicitly assigned to Harmonia;
- Harmonia cannot enforce policy, security, information governance or operational controls assigned to it.

Participation, information, integration and coordination do not, by
themselves, establish authority to determine or manage the underlying domain
activity. Assigned Harmonia operational responsibility remains applicable.

#### Examples and established specialisations (non-normative)

These examples explain the boundary; they do not expand the axiom or
establish Application Components, Information Concepts, Services, Processes,
AI allocation or implementation mechanisms.

- **Clinical work:** Harmonia may integrate and coordinate around clinical work
  without thereby acquiring authority to determine clinical work, manage
  clinical handover, own clinical worklists, allocate clinical work, make
  clinical decisions or become the EMR workflow authority. The detailed
  [Domain03 clinical-work integration boundary](../../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/metamodel/business-architecture-metamodel.md#37-clinical-work-integration-boundary)
  remains the Business specialisation.
- **Digital Twins:** A Twin may coordinate operational activity associated
  with its real-world entity without thereby acquiring authority over
  originating clinical facts or domain decisions. The
  [Strategy entity-specific coordination rule](../../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/strategic-views/logical-component-responsibilities.md#entity-specific-operational-coordination)
  remains controlling for that coordination.
- **Capacity:** Higher-order Service Capacity Management may consume
  context-specific capacity without acquiring the originating responsibility
  for Clinic, Ward, Theatre, ED, Outpatient or Mobile Service Capacity
  Management. The detailed
  [Business capacity responsibility boundary](../../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/04-health-service-operations.md#capacity-management-responsibility-boundary)
  remains in Business Architecture.
- **Assurance:** Observation, access to evidence or establishment of an
  assurance conclusion does not confer management authority over the activity
  being assured. Independent Assurance remains governed by
  [REQ-FND-005](../../requirement/bbb7438e78604308abba93afc14f4e2e.md)
  and its established
  [Strategy](../../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/capability-maps/health-service-assurance-derivation.md)
  and [Business](../../../../../docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md)
  derivation.
- **Presentation / UI:** Presentation or collection of information does not,
  by itself, confer originating information or domain-decision authority on
  the presenting component. The existing
  [Iris contextual human interaction responsibility](../../../../../docs/markdown/02-strategy/strategic-views/logical-component-responsibilities.md#component-6-iris-contextual-human-interaction)
  remains distinct.
- **AI:** Assistance with interpretation, pattern recognition, criteria
  evaluation or decision support does not, by itself, confer the authority of
  the governed actor, role or capability using that assistance. This example
  assigns no AI responsibility or capability.

#### Related architectural authority

- [AX-06](../952c3b6148ce4fce94b69f99a0c2fec7.md) governs information authority and credibility.
- [AX-13](../b6a55decfeec4f1bb3d7f18534a2ffea.md) governs the Harmonia management boundary at ingress/egress.
- [AX-14](../d3fc6025dc7646d1b2020b51f7a44bfa.md) preserves meaningful semantic distinctions.
- [AX-16](../de7e90f46127455a9ec9ad3b9b48ba54.md) governs coordinated operational activity/entity progression.
- [AX-17](8882573df7ce43c6bc0f66da0a676139.md) governs architectural authority and explicit uncertainty.
- AX-18 governs inference of domain authority from participation, information,
  integration or coordination.

findings.after:
### Assessment Summary
Assuming that internal network segments, container fabrics, or service-to-service calls are trustworthy by default leaves the platform vulnerable to lateral movement, credential abuse, and unauthorized clinical data manipulation.

### Operational Hazard
Traditional enterprise architectures frequently rely on perimeter firewalls: once a request crosses the external network boundary, all internal service-to-service communication is unauthenticated, unencrypted, and fully trusted.

In modern distributed and containerized integration environments, perimeter-only trust is hazardous:
- Compromise of a single peripheral container or gateway allows an attacker to make unhindered calls to core clinical repositories.
- Internal integration routes can bypass clinical consent rules and authorization checks because the caller is presumed to be "internal."
- Audit logs cannot prove who authorized a specific data retrieval or state mutation because individual operations lack verifiable caller security context.

### Architectural Implication & Response
- Security must be intrinsic to every governed operation rather than dependent upon voluntary caller behaviour or perimeter assumptions.
- Every internal request, service invocation, and state mutation must execute within an established, verifiable security context subject to platform-enforced security policy.
- Downstream security architecture (Domain 08) derives specific enforcement patterns, such as default-deny authorization and authenticated service communication, from governing axiom AX-07.
- **Related Driver**: [Statutory Health Information Privacy & Protection](../../../../docs/markdown/01-motivation/drivers-assessments/drivers.md)
- **Governing Axiom**: [AX-07 (Security Is Intrinsic to Managed Operations)](../principle/architectural-axiom/5de2ae2c3b794c2d9f3a14efd51d564f.md)
- **Downstream Requirements**: `SEC-001 / SEC-002` (Trusted Authentication & Default-Deny Authorization).

## Source-qualified contribution

Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/context-and-persistence-management.md` — ## Mnemosyne — Persistence Manager. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.

> **Mneme manages the information context of Harmonia activity; Mnemosyne manages
> the authoritative persistence of the information/metadata required to sustain
> that Context and reports authoritative persistence outcomes.**

Mnemosyne is Harmonia's **Persistence Manager**, with first-class responsibilities:

| Responsibility | Meaning and boundary |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Transaction oversight** | Harmonia-level oversight of persistence activity and outcome; heterogeneous services may retain their own transaction mechanics. No single physical or distributed transaction mechanism is prescribed. |
| **Persistent-service oversight and reporting** | Determine whether persistent services can fulfil Harmonia persistence responsibilities and report outcomes; this is distinct from IT/Ops infrastructure management. |
| **Shard management** | Manage shards within established semantic constraints; Mnemosyne does not independently decide a domain is semantically safe to shard. |
| **Authoritative persistence reporting** | Establish and report Harmonia's authoritative persistence outcome, preserving confirmed, degraded and indeterminate distinctions. |
| **Persistence logging** | Provide persistence-management operational logging; this does not replace Kleio Audit Capture or automatically become AuditEvent. Zero-PHI diagnostic controls apply. |
| **Compartment validation/reapplication** | Validate and reapply applicable compartments at the persistence boundary; persistence SHALL NOT strip, weaken or lose classification. Mnemosyne does not independently determine semantic applicability. |
| **Themis-owned PEP hosting** | Prevent governed persistence operations through Themis-owned enforcement; Identity-derived operations use applicable PEP-Criteria through PEP-Context. Mandatory Kleio capture uses its specifically adjudicated governed platform authority. Themis retains policy/enforcement semantics; capture-authority representation/mechanisms remain deferred. |
| **Search Management** | Perform underlying authoritative managed-persistence search and manage supporting Harmonia-level persistence search metadata. |
| **Research Metadata Management** | Manage capture, persistence, management and search utilisation of distinct AI-derived Research Metadata; derivation executes outside Mnemosyne. |

Mnemosyne atomically establishes authoritative durable state/version progression
and required durable management metadata under AX-05. **Persistence API/engine
success is not automatically an authoritative Harmonia persistence outcome.**
Service responses require the governing persistence contract and outcome oversight;
uncertainty SHALL remain explicit under AX-15. Cache state or successful Ergon
execution cannot substitute for authoritative persistence.

Persistence responsibility confers no originating clinical, information or
application ownership. The established [Clinical/C&G/O&A semantic domains](../../../../docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/data-and-persistence.md#persistence-responsibility-domains)
remain: coherent C&G governance authority, O&A partitionability preserving meaning,
and no prescribed database/service topology. Energeia may observe/report Mnemosyne
operational state under **R1.x/R2.x Observe → Report**, without acquiring persistence
management or infrastructure authority.

Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/context-and-persistence-management.md` — ## Mnemosyne Search Management. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.

**Search Management is a first-class Mnemosyne responsibility.** Mneme exposes
**Adhoc Search** at the activity/context-facing layer; Mnemosyne performs the
underlying authoritative persistence search. This does not expose its storage
implementation as an application-access path.

Search SHALL operate against **authoritative managed persistence**, without
assuming a transient cache is the complete searchable information space.
Mnemosyne MAY manage Harmonia-level search metadata for persistence-domain,
shard, persistent-service and search/index capabilities. Research Metadata is
distinct from, but usable by, Search Management. Query/result contracts,
completeness/consistency detail and physical search/index technology remain
unresolved; no distributed search algorithm is prescribed.

Source: `docs/markdown/05-information-systems-architecture/context-and-persistence-management.md` — ## Mnemosyne Research Metadata Management. Standing: Candidate — adjudicated Domain05 Step-B baseline; final Solution Architecture unapproved.

**Research Metadata Management is a first-class Mnemosyne responsibility,
distinct from Search Management.** Research Metadata supports AI-derived capture
of **"meaning" or relationships across content sets based on proximity**.

Authoritative source Content SHALL remain unchanged. AI-derived Research Metadata
SHALL remain distinguishable from authoritative source Content and metadata;
durable capture of a derived assertion does not confer source-content authority
or turn inference into observed fact.

```text
Authoritative source Content
  → appropriate governed Harmonia behavioural/execution construct
      → AI derivation outside Mnemosyne
          → distinct Research Metadata
              → Mnemosyne capture / persistence / management
                  → utilisation by Search Management
```

Mnemosyne manages the metadata and its search utilisation; the deriving AI
processing SHALL NOT execute within Mnemosyne. No specific Ergon class,
Dokimasia allocation or new execution framework is inferred. The appropriate
Harmonia construct retains governed execution/security and originating authority
boundaries. No AI framework, model/provider, vector technology, embedding
mechanism, proximity algorithm or physical index is selected. Detailed
**provenance, confidence and Research Metadata schema remain unresolved**.

Mnemosyne using the existing governed persistence mechanisms. Dokimasia's Provenance
Management ownership is distinct from physical persistence and does not create an
independent persistence subsystem. Existing authoritative-state/version/outcome,
information-authority, security and governance semantics remain intact. Reliable,
durable and timely information management remains subject to existing requirements,
including AX-05/10/11; no new SLA, storage technology, domain/shard allocation, API,
publication timing, acknowledgement or recovery mechanism is determined.

Agreed intent is recorded in the operative ADD Task; this contribution awaits explicit
Solution Architect candidate acceptance under HCRL 1.1.19-001 DR-18/DR-19. Prior
definitions, assertion standing and unresolved detailed-design matters are preserved.

> **Mneme manages the information context of Harmonia activity; Mnemosyne manages
> the authoritative persistence of the information/metadata required to sustain

Mnemosyne is Harmonia's **Persistence Manager**, with first-class responsibilities:

| Responsibility | Meaning and boundary |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Transaction oversight** | Harmonia-level oversight of persistence activity and outcome; heterogeneous services may retain their own transaction mechanics. No single physical or distributed transaction mechanism is prescribed. |
| **Persistent-service oversight and reporting** | Determine whether persistent services can fulfil Harmonia persistence responsibilities and report outcomes; this is distinct from IT/Ops infrastructure management. |
| **Shard management** | Manage shards within established semantic constraints; Mnemosyne does not independently decide a domain is semantically safe to shard. |
| **Authoritative persistence reporting** | Establish and report Harmonia's authoritative persistence outcome, preserving confirmed, degraded and indeterminate distinctions. |
| **Persistence logging** | Provide persistence-management operational logging; this does not replace Kleio Audit Capture or automatically become AuditEvent. Zero-PHI diagnostic controls apply. |
| **Compartment validation/reapplication** | Validate and reapply applicable compartments at the persistence boundary; persistence SHALL NOT strip, weaken or lose classification. Mnemosyne does not independently determine semantic applicability. |
| **Themis-owned PEP hosting** | Prevent governed persistence operations through Themis-owned enforcement; Identity-derived operations use applicable PEP-Criteria through PEP-Context. Mandatory Kleio capture uses its specifically adjudicated governed platform authority. Themis retains policy/enforcement semantics; capture-authority representation/mechanisms remain deferred. |
| **Search Management** | Perform underlying authoritative managed-persistence search and manage supporting Harmonia-level persistence search metadata. |
| **Research Metadata Management** | Manage capture, persistence, management and search utilisation of distinct AI-derived Research Metadata; derivation executes outside Mnemosyne. |

Mnemosyne atomically establishes authoritative durable state/version progression
and required durable management metadata under AX-05. **Persistence API/engine
success is not automatically an authoritative Harmonia persistence outcome.**
Service responses require the governing persistence contract and outcome oversight;

findings.after:
**Description** Information describing a formal request for a service, activity or other fulfilment to be performed, including its subject, requester, intent and requested outcome. Harmonia enforces an essential architectural rule regarding clinical requisitions and service delivery: $$\text{Order} \neq \text{Healthcare Service}$$ ```mermaid graph TD ORDER["Order
(Authoritative Requisition / Directive)"] DELIV["DeliverableHealthcareService
(Bound Service Context)"] DELIVERY["HealthcareServiceDelivery
(Information Referring to Service Execution)"] DELIV -.->|"may be requested / directed via"| ORDER ORDER -.->|"requests / directs"| DELIVERY DELIV -->|"fulfilled by"| DELIVERY ``` ### Key Semantics & Invariants 1. **Associated Request Mechanism**: An `Order` is an authoritative clinical requisition, directive, or prescription requesting the delivery of a service. It is **NOT** a mandatory lifecycle stage of `Healthcare Service`. 2. **Delivery Without an Order**: Service delivery may legitimately occur without an `Order` where business or clinical semantics permit (e.g. *Emergency Resuscitation*, *Triage Assessment*, *Direct Routine Nursing Care*, *Scheduled Facility Maintenance*). 3. **Independent Lifecycles**: An `Order` possesses its own lifecycle states (*Requested*, *Accepted*, *In-Progress*, *Completed*, *Discontinued*), owned by `Order Administration`, distinct from the lifecycle of the service delivery itself. Source standing: Established Package1 conceptual information meaning; residual qualifications in selected section remain unchanged. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/order.md` — ### 3.1 Order — A; existing Concept reused. Standing: G2 candidate contribution with only the explicitly recorded decisions approved; semantic classifications and residual questions remain qualified. - **Semantic Classification**: Assertion / Request / Direction. - **Definition**: The independently identifiable clinical requisition, directive or prescription requesting bounded activity/service fulfilment for a stated subject and purpose. - **Necessity**: OR-IR1 requires the requested work to be understood and OR-IR3 requires returned facts to correlate with the same originating Order. Package1 already establishes Order as an associated direction mechanism; this family elaborates its information responsibility rather than creates a duplicate request Concept. - **Boundary**: The Order's directive standing is attributable to its originator/context; ingestion does not certify that every submitted Order is clinically valid. Order does not establish receipt, acceptance, execution or delivery. Requested clinical responsibility for bounded work does not by itself distinguish every assessment Order from Referral; G1 U1 remains. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/order.md` — ## 1. Purpose & Semantic Boundary. Standing: G2 source-qualified boundary and unresolved questions; no whole-family approval. Order Administration needs to understand an attributable request/direction for bounded clinical activity or service fulfilment, determine its destination, coordinate routing, track a closed loop, coordinate requested modification/cancellation and associate returned outcomes. Diagnostic, medication and procedural orders remain in scope; the local diagnostic Process does not delimit the entire family. ```text Order ≠ Referral ≠ HealthcareServiceDelivery ≠ ServiceOutcome Dispatch ≠ receipt ≠ acknowledgement ≠ acceptance Modification/cancellation requested ≠ modification/cancellation effected Order closure / requester acknowledgement ≠ diagnostic-content verification ``` Reuse the [Healthcare Service semantic chain](2a791e0e1f6b45c0a57fb8233f73faa5.md): DeliverableHealthcareService → optional Order → HealthcareServiceDelivery → ServiceOutcome. These arrows distinguish meanings and evidenced associations, not mandatory states of a single lifecycle. Delivery may occur without an Order; an Order may remain unfulfilled. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/order.md` — ## 6. Temporal & Lifecycle Characteristics. Standing: G2 source-qualified boundary and unresolved questions; no whole-family approval. Closed-loop progression requires requested/issued and received time where available, dispatch time, recipient-reported occurrence/disposition time, association time and Harmonia recorded time to be distinguished. Requested timing, imaging scheduled timing and actual execution timing apply only where supplied/evidenced. A cancellation/modification request's time is distinct from an established effect time; a response delay does not determine whether the effect occurred. The local diagnostic/procedural Process preserves signed requisition, specimen/scheduling, preliminary/final result binding and requester acknowledgement/closure requirements. It does not establish a universal signature state, specimen stage or result lifecycle for medication or every Order. Its Order Dispatched compound checkpoint contains routing and recipient acceptance facts; Behaviour Received is not mapped to it without evidence (G1 U8). Foundation's illustrative independent Order states remain guidance, not an exhaustive universal state machine. Order information progression, actual service execution, returned-information lifecycle and Process checkpoint progression remain distinct. Closed / Verified concerns requester acknowledgement and Order closure; it does not establish diagnostic-content verification, approval or incorporation. G1 U2's signing/finality/legal criteria and U5's business-acceptance criteria remain unresolved. Foundation correction/provenance principles apply; the Closed-Loop Tracking Ledger label does not independently establish exhaustive retention policy. No cancellation race-resolution, retry protocol, order-entry workflow or universal completion rule is added. ## Source-qualified contribution Source: `docs/markdown/04-information-architecture/information-families/order.md` — ## 8. Explicit Boundaries, Unresolved Semantics & Downstream Realisation. Standing: G2 source-qualified boundary and unresolved questions; no whole-family approval. G2-Q07 retains who may request/authorise changes, the meaning of performing-system response and when modification/cancellation takes effect. Candidate assembly boundaries remain G2-Q06. Exact diagnostic authority/finality/legal criteria are consumed only within established local requirements, never resolved by Order Administration. No Order subtype taxonomy, universal healthcare request superclass, order-entry system, clinical verification system or unsupported Service dependency is designed. Order Outcome association has no allocated Feature identity. The assessment Referral/bounded Order semantic boundary remains unresolved rather than merged. No FHIR/resource/profile mapping, Java/application representation, schema, persistence/cache model, API, integration message, topic or implementation allocation is created. [AX-17](../../../motivation/principle/architectural-axiom/8882573df7ce43c6bc0f66da0a676139.md) governs all candidate and unestablished derivation links.

findings.after:
#### Axiom

Documented architectural decisions, definitions, relationships, boundaries
and constraints are authoritative and SHALL NOT be silently reinterpreted,
replaced, bypassed or contradicted by downstream architecture or
implementation.

Where the architecture does not establish a fact, relationship,
responsibility or decision, that absence SHALL be preserved explicitly
rather than completed through inference, convention, structural
convenience, lexical similarity or anticipated implementation.

Unresolved architecture MAY be accompanied by clearly identified
candidates, suggestions or recommendations, but these SHALL remain
explicitly non-authoritative until explicitly accepted into the
architecture.

Where evidence indicates that authoritative architecture may be incorrect,
incomplete or internally inconsistent, the conflict SHALL be raised
explicitly for architectural review. The existing architecture remains
authoritative until an approved architectural change is made. That
approved change becomes the new authoritative architecture.

#### Rationale

Downstream derivation must distinguish established architectural knowledge
from gaps and proposed resolutions. A plausible relationship supplies no
authority merely because it makes a model or implementation appear
complete. Absence of an established relationship is architecturally
meaningful information.

Repeated architectural review during Domain04 Package2 G1 confirmed this
need across different traceability relationships:

- K9: unresolved Capability hierarchy must not be completed through
  invented ancestry.
- K10: Behaviour / Process traceability must not be completed through
  invented stage equivalence.
- K11: Function / Service traceability must not be completed through
  unsupported Feature association.
- K12: cross-capability dependency traceability must not be completed
  through invented Service ownership or consumption.
- K13: downstream representation traceability must not be completed through
  anticipated FHIR, application or technology mappings.

These examples justify an architecture-wide rule; its application does
not depend on Domain04 or G1 terminology.

#### Consequences

Human architects, human developers and AI development agents SHALL apply
this axiom to architecture derivation, documentation generation and
implementation.

Architectural traceability SHALL represent established relationships and
explicitly preserve unresolved or unestablished relationships.
Completeness SHALL NOT be manufactured through:

- inferred hierarchy;
- structural convenience;
- lexical similarity;
- conventional modelling patterns;
- assumed equivalence;
- anticipated implementation;
- familiar standards;
- probable application design.

Candidates, suggestions and recommendations SHALL be distinguishable from
documented, approved architecture. A proposed resolution or apparently
better alternative SHALL NOT acquire authority through downstream use.

AI development agents SHOULD challenge architecture when evidence
warrants architectural review. They SHALL NOT silently bypass it because
they recognise a familiar destination.

This axiom applies the authority and explicit-review obligations in
[Purpose](../../../../../docs/markdown/governance/architectural-axioms.md#1-purpose), [Relationship to Architecture Decisions](../../../../../docs/markdown/governance/architectural-axioms.md#6-relationship-to-architecture-decisions)
and [Architectural Review Rule](../../../../../docs/markdown/governance/architectural-axioms.md#7-architectural-review-rule) to downstream
derivation and implementation.

[AX-14](../d3fc6025dc7646d1b2020b51f7a44bfa.md) preserves semantic
distinctions; this axiom preserves the distinction between established,
unresolved and proposed architecture.
[AX-15](../ef8abbaec37e4890ad78b9f263e67906.md) governs uncertainty
about operational state, outcome or effect; this axiom governs uncertainty
about the architecture itself. Neither form of uncertainty may be silently
resolved by assumption.

[AX-02](../eee8c3783d964d18a7f9dcea85fcd4cf.md)
and [AX-04](../54508cda80484a6caf95b901780eaf7d.md)
preserve Harmonia's internal semantics from external standards and engine
assumptions. Familiar standards or technology patterns do not establish
otherwise undocumented architectural relationships.
[AX-06](../952c3b6148ce4fce94b69f99a0c2fec7.md) governs the authority
of managed information; architectural authority remains a distinct concern.

#### Maxim

**Traceability must be truthful, not artificially complete.**
